speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, could you tell me how old you are and if you have noticed any swollen lymph nodes or an enlarged liver or spleen? Also, have you experienced any night sweats or unintentional weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Does she have any visible petechiae or small red spots on her skin, and has she had any recent infections or exposure to sick contacts? I would also like to examine her legs and abdomen for any masses or tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and easy bruising. I also have Fever, Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now examine the patient for bone tenderness, hepatosplenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work shows significant anemia, thrombocytopenia, and a very high white blood cell count, which strongly suggests acute leukemia. I need to see the actual blood cells to confirm the type, so REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal peripheral smear is unexpected given the high white blood cell count; I will proceed with a bone marrow aspiration and biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and determine the lineage of the blast cells. REQUEST TEST: Bone_Marrow_Aspirate_and_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Predominantly immature cells that are positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone marrow results confirm the presence of lymphoblasts positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT, which is diagnostic for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
